status: prepared security evidence; isolated QA-artifact backport prepared for 1.70
finding: The previous sanitizer searched compressed HTML report bytes without opening the embedded ZIP. A synthetic compressed/JSON-escaped password produces no outer raw match and therefore demonstrates a false-negative boundary. No real secret value or historical public artifact was read by this check; it does not establish an actual credential leak.
scope: Any configured primary/secondary QA username or password disables automatic screenshots, traces, video and failure input-context snapshots. Anonymous recording behavior remains unchanged; explicit post-login visual attachments retain their separate scope.

Read the pinned Playwright HTML reporter's base64 ZIP serially, sanitize raw and nested JSON-escaped credential spellings, then rebuild a valid archive instead of overwriting compressed bytes/checksums.

Bound report metadata to 4096 JSON entries, 16 MiB per entry and 64 MiB total/compressed archive. Refuse malformed encoding, unsafe/unreadable/unsupported entries and unexpected standalone credentialed archives/video so the existing upload gate fails closed.
Retain current raw-text redaction and nested-root traversal; re-check decoded report data before success. Anonymous archives remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
Extend ignore rules for local environment variants and common private-key containers, while retaining reviewable example/sample/template files. No tracked file or user credential is deleted.
primaryImplementation: Installed Playwright1.61.1 lib/runner/index.js _writeReportData/_addDataFile: base64 ZIP template and JSON entries; existing playwright-core/lib/utilsBundle exports yauzl/yazl. No new dependency or network download. This contract must be rechecked with future Playwright upgrades.

evidence: Configured quote/backslash-containing synthetic password is removed from compressed JSON; status stays failed, the report ZIP decodes successfully and a second pass preserves exact bytes.
Standalone escaped JSON, missing roots, unexpected trace/video, malformed encoding, non-JSON archive entries and oversized compressed metadata cases.
Rejected evidence remains unedited/undeleted; anonymous ZIP bytes remain unchanged.
Each of the four credential environment variables individually suppresses recordings/input context; anonymous configuration retains all diagnostic recordings.
